recognize_zh: 低倍淋巴結免疫組化中，棕色陽性細胞密集分布於濾泡間與副皮質區，而多個淡藍色圓形濾泡區幾乎不著色，顯示擴張的 T 細胞區；抗體名稱未在圖中標示，須對照 ALPS 典型的雙陰性 T 細胞（CD3+ CD4- CD8-）判讀。
features: Low-power lymph node immunostain with numerous brown-positive small cells
Positive cells concentrated in expanded interfollicular/paracortical zones, focally forming dense aggregates
Multiple round pale follicle-shaped areas largely negative
Positive cells appear small and individually dispersed without sheets of large cells
Specific antibody not indicated in the image, limiting interpretation
describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemical stain of a lymph node (antibody not specified in the image) shows numerous positive small cells concentrated in expanded interfollicular and paracortical regions, with focal dense aggregates, while multiple round follicle-like areas are largely negative. The distribution indicates an expanded T-zone or interfollicular population rather than follicular involvement. In autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome, paracortical T cells are increased and a large fraction are CD4- CD8- double-negative T cells; interpretation requires the corresponding CD3, CD4 and CD8 stains and flow cytometry.

ddx.vs: Paracortical T cells are predominantly CD4+ or CD8+, without an expanded CD3+ CD4- CD8- population.
PTCL shows atypical T cells with aberrant antigen loss and clonal TCR rearrangement, whereas ALPS T cells are polyclonal.
Neoplastic follicles are CD10/BCL2 positive B-cell nodules, unlike the negative follicles and interfollicular staining pattern here.
